status: frozen before any Stage83 arm was fitted, simulated or scored
question: Do ordinary-seat multipliers on the candidate within-remainder noise (and, separately, the major-mass noise), seat and shared parts together, fitted on earlier elections only, beat the D107-only control on the 257 historical candidate records, with flagged seats held at 1.00?
flags: Stage67 primary flags (38 of 257) and the 17-flag sensitivity set, read from data/processed/exceptional-balance-scale/design-contract.json; not re-researched, revised or extended
controlBalanceRule: every arm: candidate balance seat scale x 0.60 in seats not flagged by the Stage67 primary set, x 1.00 in flagged seats (D107); only the within and mass multipliers differ between arms

within.within: m_within earlier-trained on ordinary seats, applied to ordinary seats only

within_mass.mass: m_mass earlier-trained on ordinary seats, applied to ordinary seats only

within17.within: as within with the 17-flag ordinary set in fitting and in the multiplier assignment

within_mass17.mass: as within_mass with the 17-flag ordinary set

fit.estimator: penalty-free per-seat-normalised Gaussian likelihood on standardised total-law residuals, equal elections, ordinary seats only; closed form m = sqrt(mean over earlier elections of r_y), r_y the equal-seat mean of the realised-to-expected squared-residual ratio at the election's own Stage45 fold scales; seat and shared parts take the same multiplier
fit.withinRatio: per seat ||P e||^2 / trace(P Sigma P): e the raw within-remainder CLR residual (actual minus mean), P the centring over the non-major candidates, Sigma = seat^2 I + shared^2 T T' with T the party-tag indicator; seats with fewer than two non-major candidates or an undefined coordinate are skipped and counted
fit.massRatio: per seat e^2 / (shared^2 + seat^2), e = observed major-mass logit minus the Gaussian-logistic location of the mean (the Stage61 total-law residual)
fit.cap: multiplier = min(1, estimate): no multiplier above 1 is fitted or applied

components.harness: scripts.uncertainty_expectation.simulation.component on the Stage44 candidate records, Stage45 fold scales, common streams across arms; general electorates only

scoring.minorCandidates: candidates in the 'other' class (affiliated with a party that is not National or Labour); independents (no group) reported separately
metrics: CRPS in percentage points, equal-seat mean of the per-seat mean over the group's candidates
National and Labour candidate coverage, CRPS and 90% width
probability of the actual winner and predicted minor-party win mass against actual minor-party wins

decision.population: ordinary seats (Stage67 primary flags) in the decision years 2017, 2020, 2023; the 17-flag arms are reported on their own ordinary17 population

qualifies.sensitivity17: the matching 17-flag arm has a negative pooled minor-CRPS change and a minor 80% coverage nearer nominal than control
qualifies.precision: pooled minor 80% coverage from the first 16384 draws differs from the full 32768 by at most 0.005

decision.selection: both candidates qualify: within_mass only if its pooled minor CRPS beats within by a further relative 0.01 and it passes every guard, else within; one qualifies: that arm; none: keep_control (labelled worse if both candidates raise pooled minor CRPS, negligible if both change it by under 0.01, else mixed)

bootstrap.scheme: seats resampled with replacement within election, pooled equal-seat mean, paired against control; reported, not a gate

descriptive.leak: the Stage67 flags were assigned with every 2014-2023 result known and 21 of the 38 came from a residual-ranked list; narrowing the ordinary group is partly mechanical (about 0.72x from trimming alone, Stage67). The 17-flag arms are the check. Reference values 0.55 (within) and 0.75 (mass) were seen on all four elections before this freeze and are not pre-registered fits.
descriptive.preFreezeObservations: before freezing, the coordinator-level diagnostic (minor-party-spread-findings-2026-10-10.md) showed that narrowing mass by 0.75 in ordinary seats lowers National candidate 80% coverage from 0.731 to 0.689 (Labour 0.799 to 0.776); this is why within and within_mass are separate arms and why the major guard exists.

doNot: no arm beyond control, within, within_mass, within17 and within_mass17; no grid, penalty, prior-strength or feature search
no Student-t, mixture, regime or sigma-shrinkage; no other item on the do-not-reopen list
no flag added, removed or reclassified after any Stage83 fit or score
no mean, S, R, kappa, ratio-offset, elasticity, local-party, national, balance-multiplier or Maori change
no multiplier above 1; no change to frozen Stage44 to Stage75 outputs, scales, draw counts or tolerances
no composed bank, national MCMC, acquisition, source or data/sources.json edit
no CI, workflow or validation-registry edit; the new pipeline is exercised in CI only through its unit tests
no operational adoption beyond the config values recorded in the findings, which James signs off by merging
deviationsFromTheDraftJamesApproved: penalty-free fit (Stage67 precedent) instead of the Stage48 ridge named in the draft: the draft cited Stage67 but named a ridge Stage67 does not use
within and mass are separate arms (the draft had one joint arm) because the pre-freeze observation above shows mass narrowing trades against National candidate coverage
the composed 193-seat National/Labour width check is replaced by a candidate-only major guard (coverage and CRPS), since the composed harness needs cached national forecasts
